description: FIRST GOLDEN WITH OFFSET-SURFACE FACES (OFFSET-SURFACE-VOLUME-1). A 30-wide profile, a bottom line, two vertical sides and a 6-point sketch SPLINE across the top, extruded 10 mm and SHELLED inward 1 mm with the top face open (picked by its stage-1 face signature). The shell offsets the spline wall into a Geom_OffsetSurface (basis: the B-spline MakeThickSolid made of the extrusion), a surface type OCCT's adaptive volume rule does not converge on: before the fix the shipped integrator read +1.61 / -8.31 / +5.90 mm^3 off the truth at eps 1e-10 / 1e-12 / 1e-14, with the centroid 0.03 mm off. Converting the offset face to NURBS does not help: an offset of a polynomial surface is not polynomial, so NurbsConvert APPROXIMATES it (1.7e-6 mm off the surface) and the volume settles on a biased +6.6e-6. properties.volume_properties integrates each offset face ITSELF instead, on the TRUE surface (Gauss-Legendre per knot span over its isoline rectangle; GEOMETRY-QA 2026-09-25 F2): +1.85e-7 mm^3 in 0.1 s. OCCT's Gauss-Kronrod agrees but took 43-196 s on other shelled spline parts. The shell's loosely fitted rim edge (1.0e-5 mm) is rebuilt on the offset's exact isoline (kernel.offset_edges, GEOMETRY-QA 2026-09-25 F1), which took the reading from +1.85e-7 to -1.4e-8 mm^3 and the STEP round trip from -3.2e-7 to -1.3e-8, inside the shared ROUNDTRIP_TOL again.
derivation: EVERY MASS PROPERTY IS ANALYTIC and computed WITHOUT GProp by derive.py beside this file (re-run by tests/test_golden_derivations.py). The shell is the prism minus its cavity: the inner parallel region of the profile at distance t = 1, from z = t to z = H = 10. V = A H - A_in (H - t).

A = 405.87527732549955 mm^2 by Green's theorem on the profile (the spline is the kernel's own Edge.make_spline through the fit points; Gauss per knot span, exact on its polynomial pieces). A_in = 322.03224721038634 mm^2 by Green's theorem on the cavity boundary: the offset lines y = t, x = t, x = W - t and the spline's EXACT inward offset C(s) + t n(s), with its derivative in closed form from C' and C'', trimmed where it meets the offset verticals (bisection). Four Gauss rules up to 32 points x 8 subdivisions agree to 6e-15 relative on the volume.

volume = 405.87527732549955 x 10 - 322.03224721038634 x 9 = 1160.4625483615187 mm^3. The harness reads -1.39e-8. Before the rim edge was rebuilt it read +1.85e-7, and OCCT's Gauss-Kronrod rule +1.775e-7 at eps 1e-10 and 1e-12 alike: that plateau was the loose rim edge, not integration.

centroid from the same boundary integrals (int x dA = closed-integral x^2/2 dy, int y dA = -closed-integral y^2/2 dx; z from the two slabs) = (14.887872661020253, 6.81276499005354, 3.75123491534232). Measured within 1.65e-7 mm (y; x 3.8e-9, z 2.1e-11): the planar faces' adaptive per-face moments.

bounding_box = [0, 0, 0] .. [30, 15.018112198356267, 10]: max y is the spline's own peak (its y' = 0, by bisection). Measured: every bound padded outward by 1.0e-7, the optimal-AABB modelling-tolerance padding.

SURFACE AREA IS THE FIXED-ORDER READING, DELIBERATELY, AND IT IS KNOWN TO BE 0.681 mm^2 LOW (-2.8e-4 relative). The analytic area 2 A + P H + P_in (H - t) = 2410.1897542566303 mm^2 (P, P_in the outer and cavity perimeters by the same quadrature); the shipped fixed-order reading is 2409.5088756750556 (2409.4906214278603 before the rim edge was rebuilt: the fixed order reads the rebuilt pcurve differently), and the adaptive surface rule wanders (-18.3 / +7.85 / -0.25 at eps 1e-8 / 1e-10 / 1e-12), the offset face again. Area stays on the fixed order by the 2026-09-15 decision (properties.VOLUME_EPS docstring); if area integration is fixed, THIS value moves, and the replacement is 2410.1897542566303.

topology, hand-derived: outside, the floor, three planar walls and the spline wall (5); the open rim (1); inside, the cavity floor, three planar walls and the OFFSET spline wall (5): 11 faces, 1 shell. Edges: 4 on the outer bottom loop, 4 on the rim's outer loop, 4 outer verticals, and the same 12 inside: 24.
MESH counts are recorded, not derived, as in every golden: an exact-match determinism/regression tripwire on the 0.1 mm linear-deflection tessellation.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set. The volume sits -1.4e-8 mm^3 off its analytic truth, the centroid within 1.65e-7 mm (the planar faces' adaptive per-face moments), and every AABB bound is padded 1.0e-7 (the loft goldens' reason). 2e-7 would leave the centroid a margin of 1.2x; 5e-7 gives 3x on the centroid, 36x on the volume and 5x on the padding. The failure this golden exists to catch misses by seven orders of magnitude: the unrouted integrator's +1.61 mm^3. Loosening it requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
